This is a confirmed, currently operating facility of Rad Web Hosting in downtown Dallas, Texas. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly based on Rad Web Hosting's own published location description.

Rad Web Hosting offers shared cPanel hosting, WordPress and WooCommerce-specific hosting, VPS (KVM, cloud, and Windows options), dedicated servers, reseller hosting programs, and domain registration. The company describes its flagship Dallas facility as housed in a former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, marketed with redundant power and network connectivity; per the company's own site, it also operates additional smaller data center presences in New York City, Paris, and Tokyo, though this registry tracks only the Dallas location as a row.

This is a smaller, multi-city hosting provider rather than a wholesale or hyperscale operator, and Rad Web Hosting does not publish a specific IT capacity in megawatts, technical square footage, or year-opened date for the Dallas facility in the materials found this session, consistent with the more limited public disclosure typical of smaller hosting providers compared to the large wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. The building's history as a former Federal Reserve Bank facility is a distinctive, verifiable detail that also appears in other repurposed-carrier-hotel buildings tracked in this registry, such as Digital Realty's downtown Dallas properties, reflecting a broader industry pattern of converting older secure financial and telecom buildings into data center space. The operator markets the building heritage directly, noting the space is formerly the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, calling it one of the most secure buildings ever constructed. The facility carries a Tier 3+ designation with N+1 redundant power and cooling, biometric access control, and 24/7 on-site security, and sits on the same protected power grid segment as Dallas 911 emergency services and local hospitals. Network capacity exceeds 100Gbps across multiple Tier 1 carriers including CenturyLink and Cogent, with DDoS mitigation scaled to 1Tbps. The operator advertises the facility as powered by 100 percent renewable energy and holds SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS compliance certifications alongside its hosting, VPS, and bare-metal dedicated server offerings.

reading.body:
Rad Web Hosting operates a carrier hotel in downtown Dallas housed in a former Federal Reserve Bank building, offering shared hosting, VPS, and dedicated servers rather than wholesale or hyperscale capacity. The operator does not publish IT load in megawatts, technical square footage, or facility opening date. The facility is marked Tier 3+ with N+1 redundant power and cooling, biometric access control, and network capacity exceeding 100 Gbps across multiple Tier 1 carriers, though none of these certifications specify the total power available to the campus or the portion reserved for AI workloads.

The campus sits in downtown Dallas on a protected power grid segment serving 911 emergency services and local hospitals, and the operator markets it as powered by 100 percent renewable energy. Without a published megawatt figure, this facility cannot be ranked by AI-relevant capacity. Texas has 133 mapped facilities, only 18 of which publish capacity; the published facilities in the state total 468 MW, placing this campus below the threshold of the 18 published sites and therefore outside the state's measurable capacity pool for purposes of grid constraint analysis.

This is a smaller hosting provider with multi-city presence rather than a hyperscale operator. The absence of published power specifications means the facility makes no direct contribution to understanding either the state's AI compute footprint or the rate at which the grid is absorbing new load. Whether this property will matter to AI scaling depends on whether Rad Web Hosting publishes capacity figures or discloses material buildouts, neither of which appear in current public materials.
